title: sre-weekly-update-2026-09-05
content:
SRE Weekly Update - 2026-09-05
Owner: Aisha Malik
Summary: This week focused on stabilizing the realtime-routing regression from 2026-08-30, tuning request prioritization, and several small runbook/monitoring improvements. No site-wide outages this week; two incidents (one elevated briefly) that are now closed.

1) Incidents
- RT-2026-08-30 (Sev2) - Realtime routing regression: Symptoms: 10-15% increase in 95th/99th token latency for hosted API across us-west region during peak windows (approx 17:30-19:00 UTC). Root cause: a change in the routing policy that accidentally preferred a new model-variant pool with lower pre-warm capacity combined with an edge cache miss pattern.
  - Impact: higher tail latency for a subset of customer requests, a small number of automatic retries observed, no data loss.
  - Timeline: first observed 2026-08-30 17:22 UTC; mitigated by rollback of routing config at 2026-08-30 18:10 UTC; fully resolved following autoscaling parameter tweak and cache warm at 2026-08-31 02:00 UTC.
  - Actions taken: rolled back routing policy, reverted model-variant preference, increased pre-warm for model-variant pool, added a temporary rate-limit on experimental clients.
  - Next steps: add an automated canary check for routing changes, update rollout checklist. Postmortem draft: https://confluence.redwood.io/display/SRE/Incident+RT-2026-08-30 (linked).

- DB-2026-09-01 (Sev3) - Short-lived connection storm to metrics ingestion: caused brief missing datapoints for some dashboards for ~12 minutes. Root cause: a bug in metric forwarder retry logic combined with a transient burst from a pipeline job. Recovered automatically after forwarder backoff stabilized.
  - Actions: fixed forwarder to better handle bursts, added alert to detect missing datapoint windows >5m.

2) SLOs and Error Budget
- API generation availability SLO (99.9% p90 availability): Current rolling 30d: 99.92% (error budget remaining: ~3.5%).
- Embeddings throughput SLO: rolling 30d: 99.7% (error budget remaining: ~1.2%).
- Notes: RT-2026-08-30 consumed ~0.6% of the API error budget for the 30d window. Team action: conservative rollout of experimental routing features until embeddings SLO recovers above 99.8%.

3) On-call handoffs and rotations
- This week: Primary on-call: Tom Chen; Secondary: Priya Singh. Handoff doc updated with recent pager guidance and escalation matrix.
- Next week (2026-09-06 to 2026-09-12): Primary: Miguel Alvarez; Secondary: Laura Park. Reminder: update Slack status and team calendar before 09:00 UTC on first on-call day.

4) Runbooks and playbooks
- Updated runbook: realtime-routing-fallback (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runbooks/pull/92) — includes rollback steps, verification checklist, and rollback-to-safe-pool script usage.
- Added quick diagnostic snippet for token-latency-patterns to the SLO troubleshooting runbook.

5) Monitoring and observability improvements
- Deployed a new canary that synthetic-sends requests across model-variant pools to detect routing mis-preference within 5 minutes. Canary lives in us-west and eu-central.
- Added an alert for missing metrics ingestion windows >5 minutes (low false positive expected due to burst handling).
- Dashboard changes: added a panel for per-pool pre-warm occupancy and average cold-start count.

6) Capacity and operational notes
- Dedicated clusters: added two more nodes to ded-cluster-3 to handle expected Labour Day traffic spike; autoscaling policy adjusted to be more aggressive for pre-warm during predicted peak windows.
- Cost note: aggressive pre-warm increases short-term cost by ~4% for ded-cluster-3; justified to protect SLOs for high-value customers during anticipated peak.

7) Upcoming maintenance and planned work
- 2026-09-10 02:00-04:00 UTC: maintenance window for metrics ingestion system (rolling restarts). Will impact dashboards for up to 10 minutes per shard; alerts suppressed for planned window. Customers notified via status page.
- Work planned next week: automating canary rollback and expanding routing canary coverage to all regions.

8) Action items / owners
- Aisha: finalize postmortem for RT-2026-08-30 by 2026-09-09.
- Tom: complete canary rollback automation spike (WIP) by 2026-09-12.
- Priya: follow up and close forwarder bug PR and add missing datapoint alert (done).
- Miguel: validate ded-cluster-3 pre-warm tuning after Labour Day traffic (post-maintenance).

9) Notes / Open questions
- Request from Platform: Can we expose per-customer pre-warm telemetry for enterprise customers in the console? Needs privacy review and cost modeling.
- Question: Do we want routing policy changes to require a two-person approval for production rollout? Pros/cons to discuss in next SRE weekly meeting.

Attachments / links: Postmortem draft and runbook PRs included in linked_artifacts.

End of update.
